questions.question: Who among the following was one of the Congress leaders who drafted a Constitution for India in 1928?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Motilal Nehru.Key Points

  • Motilal Nehru was one of the Congress leaders who drafted a Constitution for India in 1928.
  •  All Parties Conference convened by the Congress Party, appointed a Committee under Pandit Motilal Nehru to draft a Swaraj Constitution for India.
  • The Nehru Committee worked from June to August 1928 and drafted a Constitution.
  • This was the first Indian attempt at Constitution-making.

Additional Information

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India CANNOT be amended with simple majority?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India CANNOT be amended with simple majority?
questions.solution: Article 21 of the Constitution of India, which guarantees the protection of life and personal liberty, cannot be amended with a simple majority. This article is a fundamental right under Part III of the Constitution and requires a more rigorous amendment process as outlined in Article 368. Simple majority amendments apply to non-fundamental aspects of the Constitution. Articles 2 and 3, related to the establishment and alteration of states, and Article 169, regarding Legislative Councils in states, can be amended with a simple majority.

questions.question: From which country has the idea of ​​rule of law in the Indian Constitution been taken?
questions.questionHtml: <font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">From which country has the idea of ​​rule of law in the Indian Constitution been taken?</font></font>
questions.solution:
The correct answer is United Kingdom.

 Key Points

  • The concept of rule of law was adapted from British common law and is enshrined in the Indian Constitution.
  • The rule of law means that no one is above the law, including the government.
  • It also means that everyone is subject to the law, regardless of their social status or position.
  • The rule of law is essential for a just and fair society, and it is one of the fundamental principles of the Indian Constitution.
  • Here are some of the provisions of the Indian Constitution that uphold the rule of law:
  • Article 13: 
    • This article states that no law can be made that is inconsistent with the fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution.
    • This means that the government cannot make any laws that violate the rights of individuals, such as the right to freedom of speech or the right to equality.
  • Article 14: 
    • This article guarantees equality before the law to all citizens.
    • This means that everyone is subject to the law, regardless of their caste, religion, gender, or any other social status. 
  • Article 19: 
    • This article guarantees certain fundamental rights to freedom of speech, assembly, association, movement, and profession.
    • These rights are essential for the exercise of the rule of law, as they allow individuals to express their views and participate in the political process.
  • Article 21: 
    • This article guarantees the right to life and personal liberty.
    • This means that no one can be deprived of their life or liberty except according to the procedure established by law.
  • The rule of law is an essential principle for any democracy, and the Indian Constitution has made significant strides in upholding this principle.
  • However, there are still challenges to the rule of law in India, such as corruption and political interference in the judiciary.

  • These challenges need to be addressed in order to ensure that the rule of law is fully realized in India.

questions.question: In the Indian Constitution, the Principle of Liberty is borrowed from which of the following countries?
questions.questionHtml: In the Indian Constitution, the Principle of Liberty is borrowed from which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
• The Principles of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity of the Indian Constitution are borrowed from the French constitution.
  • India has borrowed Directive Principles of State Policy, Nomination of members to Rajya Sabha  and Method of election of president from Ireland. 
  • India has borrowed Federation with a strong Centre, Vesting of residuary powers in the Centre, Appointment of state governors by the Centre and Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court from Canada.

questions.question: According to Indian constitution, government has how many organs?
questions.questionHtml: According to Indian constitution, government has how many organs?
questions.solution: The Indian Constitution defines three government organs: Legislature (law-making body), Executive (implements laws), and Judiciary (ensures justice). Legislature includes Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and state legislatures. Executive comprises President, Prime Minister, Governors, and ministers. Judiciary is led by the Supreme Court to uphold justice.

questions.questionHtml: As per the Constitution of India, the subject of 'livestock and animal husbandry' is included in the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is State List:

Key Points

  • As per the Constitution of India, the subject of 'livestock and animal husbandry' is included in the State List.

  • The Union list covers subjects such as defence, railways, etc., under which the laws could be made by the Parliament.

questions.question: ________ of the Indian Constitution sets qualifications for being a member of Lok Sabha.
questions.questionHtml: ________ of the Indian Constitution sets qualifications for being a member of Lok Sabha.

questions.question: The Bahujan Samaj Party was formed in 1984 under the leadership of ______.
questions.questionHtml: The Bahujan Samaj Party was formed in 1984 under the leadership of ______.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is "Kanshi Ram".

Important Points

  • Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), a national political party in India, was formed in 1984.
  • The BSP states that it represents the people at the lowest levels of the Hindu social system—those officially designated as members of the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes—as well as other religious and social minorities.
  • The core support group of the BSP consists primarily of the Dalits (Scheduled Castes, formerly called untouchables).
  • The party espouses no specific ideology, other than its opposition to and outspoken criticism of the inequalities of the caste system, and its main tenets are focused on respecting and upholding the constitutional rights of the lower members of Indian society.

Key Points

  • Kanshi Ram (1934–2006), a Dalit and a civil service worker, was spurred into pro-Dalit activism in the 1960s after reading Ambedkar’s writings and through witnessing firsthand caste discrimination.
  • Ram’s efforts to mobilize Dalits and other minorities led to his involvement in politics, in which he spent years crisscrossing Uttar Pradesh state and traveling throughout the country eliciting support for the cause.
  • In 1984 he founded the party and led it until he was succeeded by Kumari Mayawati in 2003.
  • Although Ram was responsible for building the support base for the party, Mayawati shaped and nurtured it into a powerful political force in Uttar Pradesh—India’s most populous state—and at the national level.
  • The state long remained the BSP’s stronghold, and the party also has a presence in Punjab state.
  • The first significant political success for the BSP came in 1993, when it entered into an alliance with the Samajwadi (Socialist) Party for the governance of Uttar Pradesh.
  • In 1995, however, the BSP left the coalition, and Mayawati, with support from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), became chief minister (head of government) in the state.
  • Her first term lasted less than five months until the BJP withdrew its support.
  • In the next several years Mayawati served two more short stints as chief minister: 6 months in 1997 and another 15 months in 2002–03.

questions.question: To be elected as a member of the Legislative Council, a person should not be less than __________________ years of age.
questions.questionHtml: <font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">To be elected as a member of the Legislative Council, a person should not be less than __________________ years of age. </font></font>
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 30 years.Key Points

  • Members of a State Legislative Council (MLC) must be a citizen of India, at least 30 years old, mentally sound, not insolvent, and must be enrolled voter of the state.
  • Members of the Legislative Council (MLCs) are elected for a term of six years, with one-third of the members retiring every two years
  • The elections are conducted through a system of indirect election, where members are elected by the members of the Legislative Assembly, graduates, teachers, and local authority members in the state.
  • The person should not be disqualified under the provisions of the Constitution, such as for being of unsound mind or having been convicted of certain offenses.

Additional Information

  • The State Legislative Council or Vidhan Parishad is the upper house in those states of India that have a bicameral state legislature; the lower house being the State Legislative Assembly.
  • The Legislative Council of a state is constituted as per Article 168 of the Indian Constitution.
  • As per Article 171 of the Indian Constitution, the total number of Members in the Legislative council of a State shall not exceed one-third of the total number of Members in the Legislative Assembly.
  • Of the total number of Members of the Legislative Council, 1/3 of Members are elected by electorates consisting of the Members of Local Authorities, 1/12 are elected by electorates consisting of graduates residing in the State, 1/12 are elected by electorates consisting of persons engaged in teaching, 1/3 are elected by the Members of Legislative Assembly and the remaining are nominated by the Governor.

questions.question: The model of 'Quasi Federal' form of government in Indian constitution is borrowed from which country?
questions.questionHtml: The model of 'Quasi Federal' form of government in Indian constitution is borrowed from which country?

Similarly, in India, the central government wields significant power, while states govern specific matters, creating a balanced governance model.

questions.question: When was the Environment Protection Act passed?
questions.questionHtml: When was the Environment Protection Act passed?
questions.solution: The Environment Protection Act was enacted in 1986 under Article 253 of the Indian Constitution after the Bhopal Tragedy. The Act aims to protect and improve the environment and address matters related to it.

questions.question: How many types of committees are there in the Parliament?
questions.questionHtml: How many types of committees are there in the Parliament?

options.text: None of the option is correct.
options.html: None of the option is correct.

questions.solution: Parliament has two types of committees: Standing and Ad-hoc. Standing Committees operate continuously, focusing on bills and specific subjects (e.g., Public Accounts Committee). Ad-hoc Committees are temporary, formed for specific tasks, and dissolve after completing them (e.g., Committee on Conduct during President's Address).

questions.question: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution deals with Official language?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution deals with Official language?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Part XVIIKey Points

  • Part XVII of the Indian Constitution deals with the Official Language.
  • It includes Articles 343 to 351, which outline provisions for the language to be used in the Union, States, and communication between them.
  • It also covers the promotion and development of the Hindi language and the use of English alongside Hindi for official purposes.

Additional Information

  • Part XIX:
    • This part deals with Miscellaneous Provisions of the Constitution.
    • It includes Articles 361 to 367, which cover topics such as the protection of the President
    • It Governors from legal proceedings and the interpretation of the Constitution.
  • Part XVIII:
    • This part deals with Emergency Provisions.
    • It includes Articles 352 to 360, which outline the types of emergencies in India: National Emergency, State Emergency (President’s Rule), and Financial Emergency.
    • It also describes the powers and procedures during these emergencies.
  • Part XVI:
    • This part is dedicated to Special Provisions Relating to Certain Classes.
    • It includes Articles 330 to 342, which focus on the representation of Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and other disadvantaged groups in Parliament and State Assemblies, as well as special provisions for the Anglo-Indian community.

questions.question: Which of the following is the tenure of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the tenure of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 6 years.

Key Points

  • Comptroller and Auditor General of India
    • Article 148 provides for an independent office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG).
    • The Comptroller and Auditor General is appointed by the President of India and can be removed from office only in the manner and on the grounds that a Judge of the Supreme Court is removed.
    • He is appointed for a period of 6 years or until attaining the age of 65 years whichever is earlier.
    • He is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department.
    • He acts as a guardian of the public purse and controls the entire financial system of the country at both the Centre and the state levels.
    • He primarily works to uphold the Constitution of India and the laws of Parliament in the terms of financial administration.
    • Current Comptroller and Auditor-General of India: Girish Chandra Murmu​

Additional Information

  • V. Narahari Rao
    • He was an Indian civil servant who served the Indian Audit and Accounts Service in post-independence India.
    • He served as the first Comptroller and Auditor General of India from 1948 to 1954.
    • The Government of India awarded him the third highest civilian honor of the Padma Bhushan in 1954 for his contributions to civil service.

questions.question: Right to Health is guaranteed to every citizen of India under which article?
questions.questionHtml: Right to Health is guaranteed to every citizen of India under which article?
questions.solution: The Right to Health is not explicitly mentioned in the Indian Constitution, but it is implied under Article 21, which guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty. The Indian government has also taken several steps to ensure access to healthcare as a fundamental right through various policies and programs.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT come under the Concurrent List?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following does NOT come under the Concurrent List?
questions.solution: The Indian Constitution divides legislative powers between the Centre and the States through the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List. The Concurrent List includes subjects on which both the Centre and the States can legislate, and in case of conflict, the Central law prevails. Artificial Habitats are not explicitly mentioned in the Concurrent List and are generally under state jurisdiction. Conversely, Medical Education, Protection of Wildlife, and Population Control are included in the Concurrent List, allowing both levels of government to legislate on these subjects for unified legal frameworks.

questions.question: The establishment of Union Public Service Commission, State Public Service Commissions and Joint Public Service Commission falls under which of the following features of the Constitution of India?
questions.questionHtml: The establishment of Union Public Service Commission, State Public Service Commissions and Joint Public Service Commission falls under which of the following features of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution: The establishment of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), State Public Service Commissions (SPSCs), and Joint Public Service Commission (JPSC) falls under the "Federal" feature of the Indian Constitution. These commissions are detailed in Part XIV (Articles 315 to 323) of the Constitution, emphasizing their role in maintaining and regulating public services.

questions.question: The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution does NOT exercise its control to the tribal areas of which of the following state?
questions.questionHtml: The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution does NOT exercise its control to the tribal areas of which of the following state?
questions.solution:

  • The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution provides for decentralized self-governance and dispute resolution in parts of the North East which are mainly tribal areas in the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
  • It is described in Articles 244 and 275 of the Constitution.
  • The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution does NOT exercise its control to the tribal areas of Manipur.

questions.question: Who has to resign if 'NO-Conﬁdence' Motion is passed in the Lok Sabha?
questions.questionHtml: Who has to resign if 'NO-Conﬁdence' Motion is passed in the Lok Sabha?
questions.solution: A No-Confidence Motion in Lok Sabha leads to the resignation of the Council of Ministers if passed. It is governed by Rule 198 of Lok Sabha procedures and requires the support of at least 50 members to be introduced. This motion signifies a lack of parliamentary confidence in the current government.

questions.question: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution deals with Amendment of the Constitution?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution deals with Amendment of the Constitution?
questions.solution: Part XX of the Indian Constitution deals with the amendment procedures. It outlines the process for amending various provisions to ensure flexibility and adaptability. Amendments can be initiated in either house of Parliament and require a majority vote, with some needing approval from half of the state legislatures. This part emphasizes maintaining the Constitution's fundamental framework while allowing necessary changes. Additionally, Part XIX covers miscellaneous provisions, Part XXI addresses temporary and special provisions, and Part XXII includes articles on the short title, commencement, authoritative text in Hindi, and repeals.

questions.question: Who among the following was the Secretary of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was the Secretary of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is HVR Iyengar.

Key Points

  • HVR Iyengar was the Secretary of the Constituent Assembly.

Additional Information 

  • Important facts about the Constituent Assembly
    • In 1934, M N Roy first proposed the idea of a constituent assembly.
    • The demand was taken up by the Congress Party in 1935 as an official demand.
    • The British accepted this in the August Offer of 1940.
    • Under the Cabinet Mission plan of 1946, elections were held for the formation of the constituent assembly.
    • The members of this assembly were elected indirectly, that is by the members of the provincial assemblies by the method of a single transferable vote of proportional representation
    • The constituent assembly was formed for the purpose of writing a constitution for independent India.
    • HVR Iyengar was the Secretary of the Constituent Assembly.
    • Initially, the number of members was 389.
    • After partition, some of the members went to Pakistan and the number came down to 299.
    • Out of this, 229 were from the British provinces and 70 were nominated from the princely states.
    • Dr Sachchidananda Sinha was the first temporary chairman of the Constituent Assembly.
    • Later, Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected as the President and its Vice President was Harendra Coomar Mookerjee.
    • BN Rau was the constitutional advisor.
    • On 13 December 1946, Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objective Resolution.
    • The National Flag of the Union was adopted on 22 July 1947.
    • On 24 January 1950, ‘Jana Gana Mana’ was adopted as the national anthem.
    • The final document had 22 parts, 395 articles and 8 schedules.
    • The last session was held during 14 – 26 November 1949.
    • The constitution was passed and adopted by the assembly on 26 November 1949.
    • The constitution came into force on 26 January 1950 (which is celebrated as Republic Day).

  • The constitution under Article 312 grants the Rajya Sabha (the Parliament's upper house) authority to establish new branches of All India Services with a two-thirds majority vote.
  • Article 301 of the Constitution of India about "Freedom of trade, commerce, and intercourse".
  • The Indian Penal code under Article 307.
  • Article 292 of the Constitution of India about "Borrowing by the Government of India".

questions.question: Which is NOT a unitary feature of the Constitution of India?
questions.questionHtml: Which is NOT a unitary feature of the Constitution of India?

options.text: Appointment of the Governor by the President
options.html: Appointment of the Governor by the President

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bicameral Legislature.

Key Points

  • The bicameral framework, likewise called bicameralism, is an arrangement of government in which the lawmaking body contains two houses.
  • Bicameralism is a sort of lawmaking body, one partitioned into two separate congregations, chambers, or houses, known as a bicameral council.
  • Starting around 2015, around 40% of the world's public governing bodies are bicameral, and around 60% are unicameral.
  • The Congress of the US is an illustration of a bicameral framework.

Additional Information

  • The Constitution of India provides for a federal system of government as well as a unitary system of government in the country.
  • The framers adopted the federal system due to main reasons-
    • the large size of the country
    • its socio-cultural diversity
  • However, the term 'federation' has nowhere been mentioned in the Indian Constitution.
  • The federal features of the Indian Constitution-
    • Dual Polity
    • Written Constitution
    • Division of Powers
    • The supremacy of the Constitution
    • Rigid Constitution
    • Independent Judiciary
    • Bicameralism
  • Unitary feature of the Indian Constitution-
    • Strong Centre
    • States not Indestructible
    • Single Constitution
    • The flexibility of the Constitution
    • No Equality of State Representation
    • Emergency Provisions
    • Single Citizenship
    • Integrated Judiciary
    • All India Services
    • Integrated Audit Machinery
    • Parliament's Authority over state list
    • Appointment of Governor
    • Integrated Election Machinery
    • Veto power state bills
  • Single Citizenship
    • Every individual regardless of the states or domains wherein they dwell is a resident of the country.
  • Appointment of the Governor by the President
    • An individual to be qualified for the arrangement as Lead representative ought to be a resident of India and have finished the age of 35 years (Article 157).
  • Integrated Judicial System
    • An integrated judicial system manner that decisions made with the aid of higher courts are binding on the decreased courts.

questions.question: The abolition of Dyarchy in the provinces was recommended by the ______.
questions.questionHtml: The abolition of Dyarchy in the provinces was recommended by the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e Government Of India Act of 1935,

The abolition of Dyarchy in the provinces was recommended by the Government of India Act of 1935.

  • British Parliament adopted it in August 1935.
  • This was the longest act enacted so far by the British Parliament and was later split into two parts. Government of India Act of 1935 and the State of Burma Act of 1935.
  • It extracted content from four primary sources viz. Report of the Simon Commission, discussions at the Third Round Table Conference, the reports of the Joint select committees and the White Paper of 1933.
  • The Indian Government Act of 1919 was passed to increase Indians' involvement in the Indian government.
  • Government of India Act of 1858 provided for the winding up of the Former East India Company.
  • It is called the Blueprint of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the Indian National Congress make the demand for a Constituent Assembly?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following years did the Indian National Congress make the demand for a Constituent Assembly?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1934.

Key Points

  • An idea for a Constituent Assembly was proposed in 1934 by M. N. Roy, a pioneer of the Communist movement in India and an advocate of radical democracy.
  • It became an official demand of the Indian National Congress in 1935, the Indian National Congress held its session at Lucknow in April 1936 presided by Pt. Jawahar Lal Nehru. 
  • With this, Congress added a new strand to its political engagement with the British on the future of India.

Additional Information 

  • The official demand for Constituent Assembly was raised and the Government of India Act, 1935 was rejected as it imposed the Constitution which was against the will of the Indians.
  • C. Rajagopalachari voiced the demand for a Constituent Assembly on 15 November 1939 based on adult franchise and was accepted by the British in August 1940.
  • On 8 August 1940, a statement was made by Viceroy Lord Linlithgow about the expansion of the Governor-General's Executive Council and the establishment of a War Advisory Council.
  • This offer, known as the August Offer, included giving full weight to minority opinions and allowing Indians to draft their own constitution.
  • Under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946, elections were held for the first time for the Constituent Assembly.
  • The Constitution of India was drafted by the Constituent Assembly, and it was implemented under the Cabinet Mission Plan on 16 May 1946.
  • The members of the Constituent Assembly were elected by the provincial assemblies by a single, transferable-vote system of proportional representation.
  • The total membership of the Constituent Assembly was 389 of which 292 were representatives of the provinces, 93 represented the princely states and four were from the chief commissioner provinces of Delhi, Ajmer-Merwara, Coorg, and British Baluchistan.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Banking.

Key Points

  • The Concurrent List includes subjects that give powers to both the Union and state governments to make laws on subjects included in the list.
  • The concurrent list includes subjects like Education, population control and family planning, protection of wildlife and animals, forests., criminal law, prevention of cruelty to animals.
  • Banking comes under Union List.
  • Other subjects in the Union list include defence, foreign affairs, railways.
  • The legislative functions of union and states are discussed mainly in Articles 245 to 255 in Part XI of the constitution.

questions.question: The Constitution of a country serves many purposes. Which of the following may NOT be one?

options.html: It includes that the country should uphold a Presidential form of government.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is It includes that the country should uphold a Presidential form of government.

Key Points

  • The Constitution of a country provides for the set of rules and powers for the proper governance of the Country and distributes the powers and functions accordingly.
  • It is the draft from where the government derives its powers and responsibilities and people derive their rights and freedoms.
  • It agrees on certain ideals the country should uphold.
  • Constitutions define the various institutions of government; prescribe their composition, powers and functions; and regulate relations between them.
  • Almost all constitutions establish legislative, executive and judicial branches of government.

Additional Information

  • There are a total of 25 parts in the Constitution of India in which the common articles are grouped together.
  • Originally the constitution contained 395 articles divided into 22 parts and 8 schedules.
  • At present, there are 448 articles in 25 parts, 12 schedules.

questions.question: Which of the following words in the Preamble to the Constitution describes India as a country having complete political freedom and being the supreme authority?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following words in the Preamble to the Constitution describes India as a country having complete political freedom and being the supreme authority?
questions.solution: The Preamble to India's Constitution describes India as a "Sovereign" nation, indicating its complete political freedom and supreme authority. Sovereignty means India is not under any external power and has independent legislative authority. The Preamble's keywords include "We, the people of India," reflecting the ultimate sovereignty of the people. "Socialist" and "Secular" were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, ensuring equal respect for all religions and a mixed economy. "Democratic" signifies the Constitution's authority derived from the people's will, and "Republic" indicates that the head of state, the President, is elected.

questions.question: The CADC is formed under the 6th Schedule to the Constitution of India in 1972, for the Chakma ethnic people. What does CADC stand for?
questions.questionHtml: The CADC is formed under the 6th Schedule to the Constitution of India in 1972, for the Chakma ethnic people. What does CADC stand for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Chakma Autonomous District Council.

Key Points

  • The CADC is formed under the 6th Schedule to the Constitution of India in 1972, for the Chakma ethnic people.
    • CADC stand for Chakma Autonomous District Council.

Additional Information 

  • Sixth Schedule
    • The Sixth Schedule of the Constitution provides for the administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram to safeguard the rights of the tribal population in these states.
    • This special provision for these autonomous council is provided under Article 244(2) and Article 275(1) of the Constitution.
    • Presently, 10 Autonomous Councils in Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Tripura are formed by virtue of the Sixth Schedule.
  • The Chakma Autonomous District Council
    • The Chakma Autonomous District Council is an autonomous council for the Chakma people living in the south-western part of Mizoram, India.
    • It covers the Tuichawng (Chawngte) subdivision of the Lawngtlai district.
    • Its headquarters is at Kamalanagar.
    • The Chakma people have been demanding to change the status of the Chakma Autonomous District Council into a Union territory under the name Chakmaland.
